questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following pairs does NOT have the same dimensions?
questions.explanation: Force is [M L T⁻²] while power is [M L² T⁻³], so they differ. The other three pairs match dimensionally even though they are physically different quantities.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 1: Units and Measurements

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an adiabatic process, which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: No heat is exchanged in an adiabatic change, so any work done comes out of the internal energy. That is why adiabatic expansion cools a gas.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The phenomenon of polarisation of light establishes that light waves are:
questions.explanation: Only transverse waves can be restricted to vibrate in one plane. Sound, being longitudinal, can never be polarised.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following mixtures will act as an acidic buffer solution?
options: HCl and NaOH in equal amounts
questions.explanation: An acidic buffer needs a weak acid together with its salt of a strong base, which can neutralise small additions of acid or alkali and hold the pH nearly fixed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Transition elements show variable oxidation states mainly because:
options: Their ns and (n-1)d electrons have comparable energies
They have very large atomic radii
They always lose all their electrons
Their d orbitals are completely filled
questions.explanation: Because the energy gap between 4s and 3d is small, a variable number of d electrons can also take part in bonding along with the s electrons.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 12, Chapter 4: The d- and f-Block Elements

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the strongest acid?
questions.explanation: Each electron withdrawing chlorine pulls electron density away and stabilises the carboxylate ion, so acidity rises as the number of chlorine atoms increases.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 12, Chapter 8: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In Australian Acacia the leaf is reduced and the flattened green structure that performs photosynthesis is a modification of the:
questions.explanation: This flattened petiole is called a phyllode. Reducing the lamina lowers water loss, which suits the dry Australian habitat.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Morphology of Flowering Plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Biogas produced from cattle dung is generated chiefly by the activity of:
questions.explanation: Methanogens such as Methanobacterium live anaerobically in the rumen of cattle and in biogas plants, producing a mixture rich in methane.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 8: Microbes in Human Welfare

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: A true coelom, a body cavity lined completely by mesoderm, appears for the first time in phylum:
questions.explanation: Flatworms are acoelomate and roundworms are pseudocoelomate; annelids such as the earthworm are the first truly coelomate animals.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which hormone raises the calcium level of blood by mobilising calcium from bone?
questions.explanation: Parathormone is hypercalcaemic: it stimulates bone resorption and reabsorption of calcium by the kidney. Calcitonin from the thyroid does the opposite.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 19: Chemical Coordination and Integration
